content.title: About
content.content: A tuna cake (or patty) is a ready‑to‑eat product made from whole tuna fillet mixed with a small amount of breadcrumbs, eggs and seasonings, shaped into a round patty and pre‑cooked by pan‑frying or baking. It has a delicate sea flavor, firm texture and can be served on its own or used in salads, sandwiches and burgers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the most protein‑rich and omega‑3‑rich fish species.
Tuna patties are often used in Japanese cuisine as “tuna‑patti” for sushi rolls.
A touch of starch or breadcrumbs is added during production to help the patty hold its shape.
The patty retains most of the nutrients of fresh tuna thanks to a short heat treatment.
In some countries the product is sold frozen in individual portions for quick preparation.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Tuna cake provides about 20‑25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA support heart and brain health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, tuna patty contains less saturated fat, making it a leaner choice.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in B12, niacin and B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains selenium, iodine and phosphorus, which aid immunity and thyroid function.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood may experience reactions to tuna.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Tuna can contain trace amounts of mercury; intake should be limited for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Some ready‑made patties contain added salt; check the label if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Industrial versions may include preservatives; choose additive‑free options if preferred.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the tuna patty in a skillet, oven or microwave and serve with vegetable sides, in a bun, in a salad, or thinly sliced for sushi rolls. It pairs well with soy sauce, lemon, mustard and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage freeze in an airtight bag at ‑18 °C for up to 2 months. Thaw completely before use and discard if it develops an off‑odor.
